questions.question: Although textbooks often depict cells as flat, two-dimensional diagrams, what is the actual spatial nature of a living cell?
options: They are completely flat 2D structures
They have a three-dimensional (3D) shape
They have no physical shape at all
They change between 1D and 2D shapes

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only structures that are commonly found in animal cells?
options: Cell wall, vacuole, chloroplast
Cytoplasm, cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria
Nucleus, chloroplast, cell wall
Cytoplasm, capsule, flagellum

questions.question: What defines a unicellular organism?
options: An organism consisting of exactly two cells
An organism made of a single living cell
An organism that has no cells
An organism with millions of cells working together

questions.question: In a multicellular organism, how are the cells organized to keep the organism alive?
options: Every single cell does exactly the same job and behaves independently
The organism is made of more than one cell, and different cells take on different jobs
Cells constantly destroy each other to regulate growth
Only one cell does all the work while the other cells remain dormant

questions.question: In multicellular organisms, what is formed when a group of similar cells join together to perform a specific job?
options: An organ system
An organelle
A tissue
A unicellular colony

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between tissues, organs, and organ systems?
options: An organ is a group of tissues working together to do a specific job, and organs work together in an organ system.
An organ system is made of cells only, bypassing tissues and organs.
Tissues work together to form cells, which then form organs.
An organ is a single cell that performs all bodily functions independently.

questions.question: What are the fundamental living building blocks that make up all organisms?
options: Atoms
Cells
Minerals
Tissues

questions.question: Why do we normally need a microscope to view cells?
options: Cells are too small to be seen with the unaided eye
Cells only exist when light shines on them
Cells are invisible unless they are frozen
Cells are always covered by a thick layer of soil

questions.question: Which structures are found in plant cells but are absent in typical animal cells?
options: Cytoplasm and nucleus
Cell membrane and mitochondria
Cell wall, vacuole, and sometimes chloroplasts
Nucleus and cell membrane

questions.question: When preparing a specimen slide to view under a microscope, what is the main purpose of adding a chemical stain?
options: To kill any harmful bacteria on the slide
To make it easier to see certain parts of the cells
To glue the coverslip permanently to the slide
To magnify the cell structures without using lenses

questions.question: What is the standard scientific method for recording visual observations made under a light microscope?
options: An abstract oil painting
A detailed scientific line drawing
A verbal description only
A computer-animated 3D model simulation

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of specialized cells found in animals and plants respectively?
options: Red blood cells and root hair cells
Muscle cells and bark tissues
Nerve cells and leaf organs
Skin cells and stem structures

questions.question: Which of the following lists the processes that occur in all living organisms?
options: Photosynthesis, talking, hearing, thinking, sleeping, crying
Movement, reproduction, sensitivity, growth, respiration, excretion, nutrition
Breathing, walking, eating, sleeping, reading, typing
Digesting, warming, cooling, moving, thinking, talking

questions.question: In the context of life processes, when is movement considered a sign of life?
options: When the wind blows an organism across a field
When gravity pulls a dead organism down a hill
When the organism moves itself to achieve something
When an organism is carried along by water currents

questions.question: According to biological life processes, how are all living organisms made?
options: They are created spontaneously from non-living chemicals
They are made from other living organisms when they reproduce
They assemble automatically from mineral crystals in the soil
They are formed by wind and rain erosion

questions.question: What must a scientist adjust on a light microscope to clearly observe different cell structures in a tissue sample?
options: The color of the microscope body
The stage height only
The magnification and focus
The length of the power cable
